cards.text: Paul is writing to the saints at Philippi (Philippians 1:1), and he's just finished telling them about Timothy and Epaphroditus (Philippians 2:19-30). Now he writes "Finally," and friend, this letter still has a LOT of road left. That's me yelling "LAST batch!" and then baking four more.

cards.question: Paul calls them his brothers. What does he tell them to do in the Lord?

cards.text: Then Paul admits he's about to write them the same things again. Listen, I respect a man who repeats himself. I've given this oven the same pep talk every morning for YEARS.

cards.question: Paul says writing the same things to the Philippians again is a lot of trouble for him.
What does Paul say writing the same things again is for the Philippians?

cards.text: Then Paul's tone flips HARD: "Watch out for those dogs, those workers of evil, those mutilators of the flesh!" Rejoice one second, RED ALERT the next, like me spotting a baker's sleeve drifting toward a hot oven.
Then Paul says, "it is we who are the circumcision," and he describes that group. First off, they worship by the Spirit of God.

cards.question: Paul says the circumcision worship by the Spirit of God. Who does he say they glory in?
Paul says the circumcision put great confidence in the flesh.

cards.text: Then Paul says he could have that kind of confidence himself, and if anyone else thinks they've got grounds for confidence in the flesh, he has MORE. Friend, the man just pulled out his résumé.
He was circumcised on the eighth day, he's of the people of Israel, and he's a Hebrew of Hebrews. Meanwhile MY résumé says "found at the bottom of a bin, 25 cents."

cards.question: Paul's résumé names his tribe too. Which tribe of Israel is Paul from?
As to the law, Paul says he was a ___.
Paul's résumé keeps going. As to zeal, what does Paul say he was doing?
As to righteousness in the law, Paul says he was faultless.

cards.text: Paul's résumé is stacked: tribe of Benjamin, a Pharisee, faultless in the law. He lets that sit there for a second... and then: "But."

cards.question: Paul says whatever was gain to him, he now counts as loss for the sake of Christ.

cards.text: And Paul goes BIGGER. Not just the résumé, friend. ALL things, he counts as loss, and he says he has lost all things for Christ.

cards.question: Paul counts all things as loss compared to the surpassing excellence of what?
How does Paul say he considers all the things he lost?

cards.text: RUBBISH. Paul takes the most stacked résumé in the room and treats it like an old takeout menu from my junk drawer, all so he may gain Christ and be found in Him.

cards.question: Paul doesn't want his own righteousness from the ___. He wants the righteousness from God that comes through ___ in Christ.

cards.text: Then Paul says what he wants now, and it's NOT his old title back. He wants to know Christ and the power of His resurrection.

cards.question: Paul says he also wants the fellowship of Christ's sufferings, being conformed to Him in His death.
Paul wants to know Christ in His resurrection and His sufferings. Where does Paul hope all of this leads?

cards.text: Notice the little word Paul tucks in there: somehow. I think that's a man who's done leaning on his résumé, and friend, I LOVE to see it.

findings.problem: Paul, Timothy and Epaphroditus each appear here for the first time, but none of them is introduced. Paul is never said to be an apostle or servant of Christ Jesus, and Timothy and Epaphroditus are only named.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences long: "Then Paul admits...", "Listen, I respect..." and "I've given this oven...". Only the opening card may run to three.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word Paul uses in his list (Pharisee). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out, so this tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Too many choice cards in this stop are discovery or wording guesses that can't be reasoned from the earlier cards: card 2 (rejoice), card 5 (safeguard), card 12 (tribe of Benjamin), card 13 (Pharisee) and card 14 (persecuting the church). That is 5 of the stop's 9 choice cards. Cards 12 to 14 also quiz details of Paul's list instead of the movement and meaning of the letter.

rule.text: Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Most of this card recaps Philippians 3:5-6 (tribe of Benjamin, a Pharisee, faultless in the law), which stop 1 already told and asked about. Only the final "But" moves the passage forward.
This story card is three sentences long: "And Paul goes BIGGER.", "Not just the résumé, friend." and "ALL things, he counts as loss...".

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card gives a reason for why Paul writes "somehow": that he is done leaning on his résumé. The text doesn't say why Paul uses the word. Marking it with "I think" doesn't help, because that allowance covers feelings, not reasons.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.
